subject: Clarify telemetry/cookie signal propagation & DPA scope
messages:
From: Sara Brooks <sara.brooks@acme-marketing.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Acme Legal <legal@acme-marketing.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Tracking signals / DPA scope question

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the product walkthrough last week — Acme is excited about the potential. Before we proceed, our legal and privacy teams have a few concrete questions about the telemetry that Redwood collects and processes for marketing analytics:

1) When a user on our site triggers the Redwood SDK (console + client-side events), which identifiers are included in the telemetry we send to Redwood-managed analytics? Specifically: cookie IDs, client IDs, any hashed emails, or other persistent IDs?

2) How do those signals move through Redwood's pipeline? We need to understand whether raw signals or enriched events are stored/processed outside the EU (and if so, which stages and subprocessors are involved).

3) Can we get a list of subprocessors involved in analytics and storage for Acme's account, and the geographic regions where data at rest/processing occurs?

4) Is there an option to keep telemetry processing and logs within the EU (regional routing or dedicated tenancy)? If not, what pseudonymization options do you support to reduce identifiability before data leaves the region?

We are preparing DPA language specific to tracking/telemetry and would like a short summary to share with Acme Legal. Can you send a draft DPA clause or point us to the most relevant section in your standard DPA? Ideally by EOD tomorrow — our counsel wants to start redlining.

Thanks,
Sara Brooks
Head of Growth Operations
Acme Marketing

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Brooks <sara.brooks@acme-marketing.com>
Cc: Acme Legal <legal@acme-marketing.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tracking signals / DPA scope question

Sara — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together a short summary and attached a couple of files: a cookie/telemetry signal map and our current DPA draft that includes an analytics addendum. See attachments: cookie-signal-map.xlsx; Redwood_DPA_draft_v2.pdf.

Short answers up front:
- Identifiers: by default client-side telemetry can include a client_id (SDK generated), optional hashed_email (only if you enable email hashing in onboarding), page_url, utm params, and first-party cookie values if present. We do not collect raw plaintext emails unless a customer explicitly configures that field.
- Pipeline & regions: ingestion and short-term buffering are handled in the region closest to the user by default (we support eu-west routing), but downstream enrichment and analytics jobs currently run in our centralized analytics cluster (US) unless you opt into EU-only processing.
- Subprocessors: see the attached inventory CSV; short list includes: AWS (eu-west-1 / us-east-1), Segment (US), Snowflake (US), Datadog (US), and our managed analytics cluster providers.
- EU-only options: we offer a Regional Routing add-on (keeps processing and storage in EU for telemetry & logs) and a Dedicated instance option for larger accounts. We can also enable pseudonymization (hashing + salt managed by you) before data leaves the browser/collector.

If you want, we can provide an Acme-specific redline of the DPA analytics addendum and a one-page “telemetry map” for your counsel.

Next steps: let me know which of the EU-only options you'd like cost/turnaround estimates for and I'll loop in our privacy team.

—
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Tracking signals / DPA scope question — need quick privacy review

Ben / Hannah — quick answers and suggested wording below. Happy to expand for Acme Legal if you want a cleaner doc.

Subprocessors (analytics & storage) — verified (as of 2026-09-14):
- AWS (eu-west-1 for regional routing; us-east-1 for central analytics)
- Snowflake (multi-region; account-specific replicants may be in US for our managed offering)
- Segment (US; used for ingest routing unless customer uses direct SDK)
- Datadog (US; metrics/observability only)
- Sentry (US; optional error telemetry)

Notes on signal propagation:
- Typical client-side payload (marketing config) includes: client_id (SDK cookie), page_path, utm_* params, first-party cookie values, and optionally hashed_email (SHA256) if the customer enables email capture.
- We recommend enabling client-side hashing with a customer-managed salt to minimize identifiability.
- With Regional Routing enabled, ingestion & short-term storage remain in eu-west-1; however, certain enrichment and long-term analytics jobs (modeling, joins with 3rd-party data) run in our central analytics cluster (US). We can provide a scoped contract clause to prevent long-term replication to US for Acme if they choose the Dedicated or Regional tenancy add-on.

Suggested DPA analytics paragraph (draft you can paste into the addendum):
"For telemetry and marketing analytics data (including cookies, client identifiers, and UTM parameters) processed on behalf of the Controller, Processor (Redwood Inference) shall: (i) process such data in the Controller's selected region where technically feasible; (ii) provide the option for Controller to require Regional Routing or Dedicated tenancy to keep processing and storage within the EEA; (iii) where cross-border processing is necessary, implement technical measures (pseudonymization via customer-managed hashing, encryption-at-rest, and strict access controls) and limit long-term replication to regions outside the EEA except with Controller's prior written consent."

Operational recommendations for Acme:
1) If Acme requires strict EU residence for telemetry and analytics, propose the Regional Routing add-on initially (lower lift) and Dedicated tenancy for full isolation.
2) Enable client-side email hashing with your own salt and turn off any optional identity enrichment pipelines.
3) Shorten log retention on shared analytics cluster and request an exception to exclude Acme from cross-region replication in the DPA.

I'll prepare a one-page redline of the DPA addendum and a simplified cookie/telemetry map tailored to Acme. If Ben can introduce me to Acme Legal, I can join a call to walk through the paragraph.

—
Priyom Das
Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
